clue.text: Prim clot on march, unorthodox author

indicators.note: something unorthodox departs from the usual order, so the preceding letters are set out in a new sequence

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these four words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A prissy oaf parading on a march.
explanation.walkthrough: Richmal Crompton wrote the Just William children's books; 8 down, Violet Elizabeth, is one of her characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Richmal Crompton was an English writer best known for the Just William stories about a mischievous schoolboy.

clue.text: Free admission from old writer having got cross, upset

indicators.note: in a down clue something upset is turned on its head, so the word for cross reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
a pen is a writing instrument
a rood is a crucifix, a cross

explanation.surface: A former author, annoyed, letting people in for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A rood is the cross in a church, especially one above the screen between nave and chancel.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-door policy means unrestricted entry, so the phrase describes access granted freely to anybody who comes.

clue.text: Black bird to stand in stream

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
a rook is a black crow-like bird

explanation.surface: A dark bird wading into a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To stand' is a bonus meaning: to brook something is to tolerate it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook is a small natural watercourse, a little river or creek.

clue.text: Support at lowest level

blocks.note: surface reading: a foundation or bottom stratum of some structure
setter's reading: something that props up the part of the body at the bottom, the feet

explanation.walkthrough: The words suggest engineering foundations, but the lowest level is the bottom of your body.
explanation.definitionFit: A footrest is a low stool or bar on which a seated person props their feet.

clue.text: Tricky maths, introduction to algebra, bringing complaint

indicators.note: tricky suggests something awkwardly twisted about, so the letters are rearranged
an introduction is the opening, so only the very start of the next word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of algebra

explanation.surface: Difficult mathematics, starting with algebra, gives a pupil a headache.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here means an illness or ailment, and asthma is a chronic respiratory disease.

clue.text: Greek character recently finding a hobby

blocks.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
synonym

explanation.surface: Someone from Greece who has newly taken up a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Philately is stamp collecting, a classic pastime pursued for pleasure.

clue.text: Compassionate tone when fellow is imprisoned

indicators.note: a prisoner is shut inside walls, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: a hue is a shade or tone of colour
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A kindly voice used when a man is jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means showing kindness and mercy, the same sympathetic concern for suffering.

clue.text: Be vile zealot and hit out - it's in one's character

indicators.note: hitting out is lashing about wildly, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters of these words except the connecting and

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour and lashing out are just part of someone's nature.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Elizabeth Bott is the lisping spoilt girl in the Just William books by 1 down, who threatens to 'thcream and thcream'.
explanation.definitionFit: Violet Elizabeth is a fictional figure from Richmal Crompton's stories, so she is literally a character in a book.

clue.text: Without hesitation, wicked and overbearing

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: impious means lacking reverence, wicked
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone bossy and wicked who never pauses before acting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' reads like 'unhesitatingly', but 'without' means outside: the wicked word surrounds the pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperious means domineering and arrogant, expecting to be obeyed like a ruler.

clue.text: After 60 minutes, see one beautiful maiden

blocks.note: sixty minutes make an hour
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An hour later you will meet a lovely young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition a houri is one of the lovely virgins of paradise; loosely, any alluring young woman.

clue.text: Put on clothes-line, maybe, in den

blocks.note: first meaning: to peg washing up to dry
second meaning: a place where people habitually gather

explanation.surface: Pegging out laundry inside a small room.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangout is a favourite haunt or lair, the same idea as a den where friends gather.

clue.text: Case of vintage deposited in foyer

indicators.note: something deposited in a place is placed inside it, so one word is set within the other

blocks.note: a foyer is an entrance hall
vintage things are old

explanation.surface: A crate of fine wine left in a hotel lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft travelling bag, a type of luggage or case.

clue.text: Eagerly making an attempt - and ultimately winning

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: a go is an attempt
the final letter of winning

explanation.surface: Keenly having a try and finally coming out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means in a state of keen anticipation, impatient and excited, which can stand adverbially for eagerly.

clue.text: What may be in store in French region

blocks.note: first meaning: a section of a large shop
second meaning: one of the administrative divisions of France, the département

explanation.walkthrough: 'In store' suggests something awaiting you in future; here the store is a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Big shops are divided into sections selling different goods, and France is divided into numbered administrative areas with the same name.

clue.text: Still agreeing initial bill should be ignored

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so those letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: acquiescent means assenting, going along with something
AC, short for account, is a bill; it sits at the start

explanation.surface: Someone still consenting once the first invoice is overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiescent means at rest, inactive or dormant, which is the adjective sense of still.

clue.text: Sound of cat getting back into bed - wicked!

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the cat noise is read from right to left
getting into something means entering it, so one piece ends up inside the other

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
a contented cat purrs

explanation.surface: The cat jumps back on the bed again, the naughty thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of' here just means the noise a cat makes; it does not signal a soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt means morally depraved or dishonest, sharing the sense of evil with wicked.

clue.text: Officer's unit left behind mountain pass

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the words before it are placed after the word that follows it

blocks.note: a col is a gap between peaks
one is a single unit
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A soldier's company stayed behind at a pass in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' places the unit and left after the pass, and the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army officer ranking above a lieutenant colonel.

clue.text: Note needlework round front edge of tablecloth

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the needlework word wraps around the single letter
the front edge is the leading border, so only the first letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: crochet is needlework done with a hooked needle
the opening letter of tablecloth

explanation.surface: Someone stitching a lacy trim around a tablecloth's border.
explanation.walkthrough: Crochet edging on a tablecloth is so natural that 'Note' hides as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note lasting one beat, called a quarter note in American usage.

clue.text: I recount suffering, becoming excessively depressive

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so its letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone telling of their troubles and sinking ever lower.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurotic describes someone prone to abnormal anxiety and gloom, overly troubled in mood.

clue.text: Where hay in transit may be keeping dry

definitions.text: Where hay in transit may be

blocks.clueFragment: Where hay in transit may be
blocks.note: first meaning: literally loaded on a farm cart
second meaning: abstaining from alcohol

explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping dry' seems to continue the hay picture, protecting it from rain; it actually means staying teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means abstaining from alcoholic drink, from the water cart once thought to tempt only the sober.

clue.text: Cartoon character is fool repeatedly shown up

indicators.note: in a down clue something shown up is turned upwards, so the letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: a nit is a fool, and 'repeatedly' doubles it

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure keeps being exposed as an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Nit is British slang for a silly person, short for nitwit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintin is the boy reporter hero of Hergé's Belgian comic-strip adventures.

clue.text: Tending to discriminate against another generation as I get doddery

definitions.text: Tending to discriminate against another generation

indicators.note: doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the preceding letters wobble into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An older person admits growing prejudiced against the young as frailty sets in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageist means prejudiced against people on grounds of how old they are.

clue.text: Thrill created by half-visible predatory birds

indicators.note: if only half can be seen, the other half is missing, so the latter part of the word is cut

blocks.note: buzzards are birds of prey

explanation.surface: The excitement of glimpsing hawks partly hidden in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzz is informal for a feeling of excitement or a kick, the same sense as a thrill.

clue.text: Skilful but lacking poise in exercise

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter for poise is removed

blocks.note: an expert performer is skilful
P is the symbol for the poise, a unit of viscosity

explanation.surface: A capable gymnast without composure while working out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poise' looks like grace or balance but is the physics unit of viscosity, symbol P.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert power or influence is to exercise it, bringing it to bear actively.

clue.text: Criticise a revolutionary for flamboyance

blocks.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
taken as written
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: Attacking a radical for being showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is dash and stylish confidence, a showy flair.

clue.text: Dandy - foremost of comics with nothing wrong to rake through

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so the first letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of comics
O is zero, nothing
X is the mark for a wrong answer
to comb is to search thoroughly, like raking through

explanation.surface: A leading comic paper, The Dandy, unimpeachable to rummage through.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dandy was a famous British children's comic, which is why 'comics' follows so naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a vain, conceited man overly fussy about his appearance, much like a fop.

clue.text: One of those known to be a vegetable

blocks.note: first meaning: from the idiom for an expert, someone who knows their stuff in this plural form
second meaning: a pungent bulb used in cooking

explanation.walkthrough: An expert is said to 'know their onions', so the first half is one of the things such a person knows.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom makes this bulb a thing proverbially known by experts, and it is also a common pungent kitchen staple.

clue.text: Flavour due to second fruit - minimum on front of tongue

indicators.note: the front is the leading part, so only the first letter of the following word is kept

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a pear is a fruit
min is the short form of minimum
the opening letter of tongue

explanation.surface: A taste on the tip of the tongue from another piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a kind of mint used to give a fresh taste to gum and toothpaste.
